text: Every plate begins with a guide, drawn lightly in pencil.
A chambered shell. It grows by adding rooms, one at a time.
Cut it open, and the spiral is a record: each chamber sealed off as the animal outgrew it.
A thin tube, the sigh-funkle, runs through every wall.
sub: A thin tube, the siphuncle, runs through every wall.
asr: A thin tube, the siphonkel, runs through every wall.

text: A garden snail coils its shell too.
A sunflower packs its seeds in spirals: thirty-four one way, fifty-five the other.
A young fern keeps its tip rolled in a coil until it is ready to open.
Four makers, one shape. Not the same curve, but the same habit: grow outward, and keep what you made.
